acts.title: Security
acts.narrative: I learned security by doing the whole loop: attack, defend, investigate. I ran Lockheed's Cyber Kill Chain against lab targets, performed a Blueborne exploit on a vulnerable Android phone with Kali running on my own device, and pentested web applications with OWASP ZAP and Burp Suite, from DVWA to a live ASP.NET app. I wrote my own Python malware, obfuscated and encrypted it, then took it apart again with Ghidra and IDA to learn x86 from both sides of the fight. I hardened a CentOS file server with OSSEC, firewalld, a host IPS, ACLs and BIOS encryption, configured Palo Alto next-gen firewalls and VPN tunnels, and worked EnCase, Autopsy, FTK Imager and Memoryze through a full forensics case study. In my own time I run Suricata, Snort and Zeek.

skills.name: Web application pentesting
skills.detail: OWASP Top 10, OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite

acts.title: AI & Automation
acts.narrative: Python has been mine since December 2016: Twilio, TensorFlow, Keras, Pandas, smtplib, sockets, cryptography. In 2020 I went deep on deep learning. I trained more than 40 CNN models to reach roughly 70% accuracy on food classification and emoji prediction, built an RNN autocorrect judged on word error rate, and published both write-ups. The same instinct now earns its keep at work: at Singtel I automated Akamai WAF reporting, turning alerts, logs and traffic data into reports analysts actually read. Underneath it all sit boring, load-bearing foundations: object-oriented programming in C# and functional programming.

skills.name: Python
skills.detail: Twilio, TensorFlow, Keras, Pandas, smtplib, cryptography, sockets

acts.title: Founder
acts.narrative: CiTaDel started as a conviction that SMEs deserve industry-grade defence at a price they can pay. For three years I ran it: an affordable, open-source SOC with EDR and SOAR at the core, SOC solution cost down 80%, threat detection up by as much as 90%, and deep learning folded into SOC workflows to cut false positives by 20%. The founder muscle came from Genesis, where I served as Vice-President of Startup and was nominated into the Zero to One entrepreneurship program with Meet Ventures and NUS Business School. CiTaDel wound down in May 2026 when I joined Singtel; the lessons did not.

faq.question: What does a Forward Deployed AI & Automation Security Engineer do?
faq.answer: I sit with Singtel's managed security services business and build customised AI and automation solutions for the SMEs it protects. Forward deployed means I work close to the customer problem rather than in a back room: understand the security workflow first, then automate it.

faq.question: You work full-time and study at the same time?
faq.answer: Yes. I am reading Information Security at NUS (Bachelor of Computing, Aug 2024 to May 2028) while working at Singtel. The degree finishes in 2028; the work does not wait for it.

faq.question: What are you open to?
faq.answer: Good conversations. I am settled at Singtel and NUS through 2028, and I stay open to security community work, CTFs, speaking, and hard problems in AI and security operations. Email is the fastest way to reach me: zurielst@u.nus.edu.
